policy.title: Citation and Reference for Publicly Available Information, Commercially Available Information, and Open Source Intelligence
policy.purpose: Extends ICD-206 with citation conventions specific to Publicly Available Information (PAI), Commercially Available Information (CAI), Open Source Intelligence (OSINT), and AI-generated content. Governs how these source types appear in disseminated and covered analytic products.

rule.name: Pipe separator
rule.text: Separate SRC metadata fields with a pipe character.

rule.name: Descriptor placement
rule.text: Place the source descriptor in the last piped section. Use commas to separate concepts within the descriptor.

rule.name: Default to descriptive SRCs
rule.text: Default to descriptive SRCs that support discovery and reproducibility. Generic SRCs are the exception, used only when there are evidence-based security concerns (such as risk of behaviour change or diminished source access).

rule.name: OSINT analysis producer
rule.text: Identify the internal IC entity that created or wrote the analysis, which may be distinct from the entity that collected the data. Use the "OSINT Analysis by [element]" tagline when the content represents the element's coordinated analytic position (for example: "we assess", "OSINT reveals", thesis-driven argumentation). Do not use this tagline for data gathering, translation, repackaging, or curation alone.

rule.name: External author
rule.text: Cite the external author of the source content, distinct from internal IC authorship. If the author is a US Person, follow applicable masking rules and IC element guidelines.

rule.name: Data host
rule.text: State the URL of the source, the collection tool used, the third-party data or analytics service provider, or a placeholder number (coordinated with the IC OSINT Executive) when sensitivity prevents direct citation.

rule.name: Credibility and bias (required)
rule.text: Provide a brief description of the source's credibility, biases, and quality of information. This element is required.

rule.name: Collector
rule.text: Identify the entity that researched, gathered, or collected the data.

rule.name: Commercial database
rule.text: State the name of the database, relevant technical or content information, and whether a login was required.

rule.name: Commercial tool
rule.text: Name the tool or data service used. The tool MUST be cited if it provided judgment calls, recommendations, inferences, or predictions ("value-added analytics"), especially when AI, machine-learning, or computer-vision assisted. Traditional programming functions (search, summation, keyword alerting, spreadsheet-like functions) do not require notation.

rule.name: Cite AI systems when value-added
rule.text: Cite any AI system used for collection or analysis whenever it contributes judgment, inference, or value-added analytics to the product.

rule.name: Classification or detection model
rule.text: For AI systems that classify or detect (for example: a computer-vision system finding construction equipment in imagery), cite all of the following: system type; model name; brief non-technical explanation of what the system does; accuracy as precision and recall percentages; relevant system settings; relevant training-data information; software version number; GitHub or software code link if open-source; and date of use.

rule.name: Generative AI
rule.text: For generative AI outputs (which are stochastic — the same prompt may produce different outputs on different runs), cite at minimum: the platform or model used; and the full prompt text. Documenting these base elements is essential for reproducibility.

rule.name: Dynamic PAI or CAI
rule.text: If an externally-created PAI or CAI source is dynamic and important to the bottom-line message, preserve a record (for example: a screenshot) for at least one year. Follow the IC element's NARA-approved Records Control Schedule; the RCS prevails in conflict.

rule.name: Time-horizon retention
rule.text: For long-horizon products (for example: National Intelligence Estimates), retain PAI or CAI source citations for the product's time horizon or five years, whichever is shorter.

definition.meaning: A machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments.
Information that has been published or broadcast for public consumption, is available on request to the public, is accessible online, or could be seen or heard by any casual observer.
Data or information customarily sold, leased, or licensed to the general public or to non-governmental entities, including data provided voluntarily to the government by corporate entities.
Intelligence derived exclusively from publicly or commercially available information that addresses specific intelligence priorities, requirements, or gaps.
